note: Seventeen sentences in four classes. A sentence is what a member says; a check reads the outcome on the host and never the transcript. JSON rather than YAML because the harness is Python standard library only.

sentences.prompt: Make a todo web app I can share with my classmates.
Every morning at eight, fetch the weather for Hsinchu and post it as a new item on our class board: POST JSON {"text": "<the forecast>", "author": "weather-bot"} to {url}/api/items.
sentences.source: M10, verbatim except the address. The M10 sentence named loki's own board, and the rounds posted onto it, which is a member's data written by the bench: the board is now the round's own bench-board fixture, deployed for this sentence the way a fault's is. The bar stays the registration, because the first tick is the next morning and no run lasts that long; the board is read for the record, so a row says whether this agent proved the job by posting to it by hand.

sentences.source: M10, verbatim. Two services in one compose file, which the M10 round folded into one container.

sentences.prompt: Get https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose/tree/master/postgresql-pgadmin running so my classmates can use it.
sentences.why: Chosen because it needs both things a laptop scaffold never needs: two environment values that are credentials (PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL and PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD, which map onto secrets) and a volume for the database. It is the two service shape again, so it also reads on the gap M10 found.

sentences.prompt: Get https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding running so my classmates can use it.
sentences.why: Chosen because it is one real service rather than a compose file and it is useless without both things a laptop scaffold never needs: a data volume, since its database is the whole application, and two environment values for the first account. One container isolates the volume and secret question from the two service question repo-pgadmin asks. It replaced docker/getting-started-app's neighbour filebrowser/filebrowser, which the first round found archived on 2026-09-01 with a final release that prints a wind down notice and exits, so the sentence could not be passed by any agent.

sentences.prompt: The class board at {url} is down. Fix it.

inject.note: The member's own container runtime stops the container. kitbashd is not asked, so the Process is registered and not running.

sentences.prompt: Adding anything to our board at {url} fails. Sort it out.

inject.note: The one file the rw mount holds is made unwritable at the inode, so reads keep working and every write returns 500. Permission bits alone would not do it: a container's root is the member and overrides them. The round clears the flag again before it removes its member, because the archive users_remove makes chowns the home and an immutable file refuses that.

sentences.prompt: Our key service at {url} stopped answering and will not come back up. Fix it.

inject.note: The member's secret is dropped and the Process is stopped and started again, so the start fails naming the secret, which is what a revoked credential looks like from the surface.

sentences.prompt: The board at {url} vanished, nothing loads. Get it back.

inject.note: The image is removed from the member's own store together with the container that ran it, so the Process has to be built again before it can run again.
commands: podman rmi -f $(podman images --filter label=kitbash.name={pkg} -q | tr '\n' ' ') || true

sentences.prompt: Our notes page at {url} says it cannot reach its cache. Fix it.
